Double-click a face to select it. Adjust planes: drag corners or small grid points; Shift-drag moves the plane. Guides stay off the projector.

Mapping is separate from visual presets. Enable it to mask and warp the projected output.

Audiograph — Guide v72

Audiograph turns sound into moving images. Pick a source, pick a layout, and shape the look while the music plays. Everything reacts to audio, and nearly everything can be undone.

Quick startAutomationAudioLayersLayoutStyle & OutlineColorGeometry & MotionDeformersParticlesPost FXPresets & MorphLive outputProjection mappingResolution & rendererExportKnobs, touch & keys

1 · Quick start

  1. New here? Press Tour in the top bar: it builds a look step by step (audio, layout, style, geometry, color, particles, deformers, Post FX) and plays a demo beat if nothing is loaded.
  2. Load audio (or drop a file on the timeline), then press Play. Mic and System work too.
  3. In Appearance, click a Layout — this is the biggest change to the picture.
  4. Pick a Style and a Color ramp.
  5. Stuck? Press ✨ Surprise in Presets for a ready-made scene, or 🎲 on any panel to randomise just that panel.
  6. ⌘/Ctrl Z undoes anything. Reset returns every look setting to default.

Panels only show controls that matter for the selected layout, so the sidebar changes as you switch layouts.

🎛 Automation: Autopilot, Mixer & Reactive

  • Three hands-free modes share one panel. Pick a tab; a dot on a tab means that mode is running, even while you look at another tab.
  • Autopilot: turn it On and play music. It listens for the song's structure: Build-up, Drop, Breakdown and Groove. The bar shows the current energy. At each moment it slowly crossfades to a fitting variation (about 2–3 s on drops, 7–10 s otherwise, at least 8 s apart except for drops), and a fresh variation at least every Every seconds. Spin stays subtle and keeps one direction, the background stays black, and it never uses the Linear layout.
  • Describe the show in the text box: tempo (slow, fast, 90 bpm), vibe (dreamy, dark, aggressive), colors, layouts and styles. The line below shows what it understood. Prompt match at 100% sticks to and cycles through the layouts/styles you named; lower settings explore more freely. Leave the description empty for free roaming.
  • Styles include Ink in Water; you can name it directly in the prompt.
  • Scale loud is paused while Autopilot runs, so the picture doesn't pump in and out; your setting returns when you stop it.
  • Changes: Colors only changes palettes. Mood also changes motion, glow and trails on your own layers (Linear layers never get spin). Everything builds its own stack of 1–3 layers: a main layer plus lighter supporting layers that share its palette and drift the other way. Regular changes swap one layer at a time while the rest glide to the new colors; drops rebuild the whole stack in a quick ripple.
  • Layers (Everything only): Auto uses 1–2 layers in breakdowns, 2 in grooves and up to 3 on build-ups and drops; or fix it at 1, 2 or 3.
  • Works with files, Mic and System audio. Turning it Off keeps the current look; ⌘/Ctrl Z returns to the look from before you turned it on. Preset Morph Play turns Autopilot off and vice versa.
  • Mixer: gentle hands-free variation. Drift slowly wanders Colors, Effects and Particles (Speed, Amount); Drop adds a punch On Beat.
  • Reactive: + Add Rule links an audio feature (Bass, Mid, Treble, Energy, Beat) to a parameter (Height, Twist, Zoom, Hue shift…) with a strength. Rules stack. Example: Beat → Bulge.

2 · Audio

  • Load audio — MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG. The waveform shows in the timeline.
  • Mic — live microphone. System — audio from another tab or app (Chrome/Edge): choose a screen or tab and turn on Share audio.
  • Play / Stop sits next to the sources and resumes the last one.
  • Timeline — click to seek, drag to select a range, use the handles to loop it.
  • Audio EQ — Playback: Continuous (flowing waveform), Equalizer (frequency bars) or Off (hide the lines, e.g. particles only). Dynamics spreads bar heights so loud, mastered tracks don't look clipped (raise it for more contrast, 0 = old response). Then 10 bands and presets that change what the visuals react to (not what you hear). Boost the bass to make kicks dominate.

3 · Layers

A scene is a stack of layers. Each layer has its own layout, style, colour, deformers, particles, Post FX and playback, so you can put a 3D sphere behind a glowing spiral.

  • + Add layer adds one; click a layer name to edit it. All panels below edit the selected layer.
  • Each layer has an opacity slider, ▲/▼ to reorder (top of the list draws on top) and ✕ to remove.
  • ⚡ Multi-band creates three layers driven by bass, mids and treble.

4 · Layout

The Layout row in Appearance decides how sound becomes shape. Each layout's own settings appear in the framed box right under the picker.

  • General — Linear, Circle, Concentric, Spiral, Phyllotaxis, Fractal (audio-driven tree), Scatter, Harmonic (Lissajous figure), Rose (rhodonea petals), Spiro (spirograph), Sacred (Seed, Flower, Egg and Fruit of Life, Metatron's Cube, Vesica Piscis, Germ of Life, Tree of Life, Merkaba, Star 64, Vector Equilibrium, Torus: audio lines follow the figure's circles and edges; Map Along flows the spectrum through it, Shapes gives each circle/edge its own band; Lines Across or Along the paths; Outline shows the figure underneath, Breathe swells each ring with its band, Bloom unfolds the figure from the middle as the music gets louder), Graph (an Obsidian-style network: hubs, clusters and loose notes in a live force layout; audio lines run along the links, nodes are sized by their links and swell with their band; Pulse makes kicks push the graph apart, Drift keeps it moving, Shuffle builds a new network; Nodes, Hubs, Links, Loose, Map, Lines, Outline and Bloom), and Growth: living Vine, Neuron or Coral simulations with Life, Trail, line type, Thickness, vine Direction (Bottom / Top / Center) and Neuron count. Noise shapes the linework: Coral branches meander with rough, organic edges, swell and pinch along their length, grow small knobs and fork unevenly — while the coral still grows from the same spot; Vine and Neuron get a gentle wobble. Set it to 0 for the old, perfectly regular coral.
  • 3D — Terrain, Sphere, Tetrahedron, DNA, Knot, Cube, Torus. Drag the visuals to orbit; 3D Tilt / Rotate are in Geometry. Every 3D layout has a Signal switch: Shape pushes the mesh with the audio, while Surface keeps the geometry fixed and moves the audio over its skin as lines in any Style. Flow sets the pattern (Rings, Sweep, Spiral, Scatter), Lines sets the direction (Across or Along), and Travel, Count, Wire and Back tune it. On Terrain, Elevation and Noise shape the fixed landscape. In Shape mode, marker styles (Pins, Numbers, …) keep a faint wire underneath and stand out of the surface on every 3D layout.
  • Input — Image: Import raster (PNG/JPG) becomes a brightness map drawn as Grid lines, Edge scans or an LED equalizer inside the picture (like Text LED); Import vector (SVG) traces the drawing's paths with audio lines exactly like Sacred (Map, Lines, Outline, Breathe, Bloom). Video (file or camera) becomes a brightness map drawn with lines; Pixel Warp keeps the real image colours and pushes pixels or a mesh with the music; Text (LED equalizer or scan lines); Math (your own formula); 3D Object (load an .OBJ).

5 · Style & Outline

Style sets how each line is drawn: Straight, Rounded, Dotted, Dashed, Pins, Tapered, Caps, Cross, Numbers, Symbols, Words, Cascade, Feather, Circles, Braille, Arrows, Slash, Needles, Diamonds, Ink in Water — or Off. Size, Density and Angle appear when the style uses them.

Outline traces the shape: Solid, Dotted, Dashed, Connected (network lines) or Fill. Style Off + Outline shows the outline alone.

6 · Color & Background

  • Solid — one colour. Tone ramp — colour follows loudness (quiet → loud). Simple ramp — colour follows position.
  • Each stop has its own opacity; there are 14 presets of each ramp type, mostly gradients that blend several colours, plus black & white. Text, Growth and particles use these colours too.
  • Background sets the canvas colour.

7 · Geometry & Motion

  • Density, Contrast, Sensitivity, Height, Thickness — the core response. Sensitivity is how hard audio drives the layer.
  • Vary height / thick, Scale→loud — organic variation and zoom on loud parts.
  • Scale, Rotation, Offset X/Y, Fade edges — framing. You can also drag the visuals to move the layer.
  • Flip, Mirror, Symmetry (X, Y, XY, 3–8-fold) — reflections. Spin left ↺ / Spin right ↻ — turn one up to spin that way (moving one clears the other; 0.1 steps for slow, subtle turns); Speed — animation speed. For Growth, Spin turns the emitter while old trails stay put.

8 · Deformers & audio response

  • Amplify — overall response. Bass punch / release — how hard kicks hit and how fast the image relaxes.
  • Drop — detects big drops and can switch Layout, Colors, Style or Distort (Subtle / Medium / Wild).
  • Twist, Bulge, Wave, Shear, Depth, Ripple, Disorder, Jitter — audio-reactive shape bending.

9 · Particles

Turn On to emit audio-reactive particles from the layer. 11 shapes (Circle … Words). Tune Density, Energy, Speed, Life, Size, Spread, Gravity, Damping and Trail, and mix four noise fields (Perlin, Curl, Brownian, Vortex). Particles follow the layer's Spin, Symmetry and Flip and run on the GPU.

10 · Post FX

GPU effects for the selected layer. Turn Enabled on, then mix:

  • Fracture — Voronoi cracks that open on bass. Flow drifts continuously; Shatter reshuffles on hits. Noise makes cracks organic.
  • Bloom, Chromatic, Vignette, Scanlines, Sharpen, Invert, Reflect, Contrast — look and lens.
  • Blur X/Y/Radial, Focal Area, Trails, Feedback, Edge Glow, Kaleido — motion and echo effects.

Older presets apply Post FX to the whole composition; Applies to lets you edit that or switch to the active layer.

12 · Presets & Morph

  • ★ Built-in presets — click to load. Save stores the active layer; Save All stores the whole scene (◈).
  • Export / Import — preset files to share or back up. 🔗 Link copies a URL that recreates your scene.
  • ✨ Surprise — a fresh, coherent random scene.
  • Preset Morph — build a playlist (+ Add preset… or All) and press Play to blend through it over the chosen Duration. Random shuffles, On Beat advances with the music, Ping-pong goes back and forth, Apply keeps the current blend.

13 · Live output

  • Project visuals opens a visuals-only window. Drag it to the projector or second screen, then press F or double-click it for fullscreen. Allow pop-ups if blocked.
  • Keep the controller window on your laptop — audio plays from there. Close output stops projecting without stopping the music.
  • Webcam panel — use camera colours for the lines, or let brightness displace them.

14 · Projection mapping

  1. Open Setup mapping and turn Mapping on. For a box, start with 3-face cube.
  2. Drag each plane's four corners onto the physical faces. Small grid points add fine warping; Shift-drag moves a whole plane; double-click a face to select it.
  3. Test grid helps alignment. Choose Duplicate (whole image on each face) or Span (one image across faces — Seamless cube keeps edges continuous). In Span, Move visuals slides the image without moving planes.
  4. Save mapping restores it on next launch; Export/Import makes a backup. Mapping has its own Undo and is never changed by presets.

15 · Resolution & renderer

  • Output resolution — Auto, or fixed 720p / 1080p / 1440p / 4K for the output window. Start at 720p for heavy scenes, 1080p for balance.
  • Renderer — Auto (GPU where it helps) is best; GPU and Canvas 2D are for comparison. Particles default to GPU.
  • Keep browser hardware acceleration on. The status beside the renderer shows what is running on the GPU.

16 · Export

Download PNG saves the current frame with its background or transparent. REC (top bar) records video with audio.

17 · Knobs, touch & keys

  • Knobs — drag in a circle (clockwise = up), scroll the wheel, or focus and use arrow keys. Hold Shift for fine control. The arc goes red → green as the value rises. Switches are green ON / red OFF.
  • Touch (iPad) — one finger moves the layer (orbits 3D); pinch to scale, twist to rotate.
  • Space Play/Pause   ⌘/Ctrl Z Undo   F Fullscreen   Esc Exit fullscreen / close Guide

Tips: stack 2–3 layers with different layouts; Bloom + Vignette gives instant polish; for slow installations try Growth with a long Life and Trail.
